instructions: Rinse 1 1/2 cups of jasmine rice under cold water until it runs mostly clear. Transfer it to a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups of water and bring it to a boil. Cover, turn the heat to the lowest setting and cook for 12 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on until you serve.
Meanwhile, trim the lemongrass to the pale bottom part and peel off the tough outer layer. Mince it as finely as you can. That should be about 1/2 cup. Mince the garlic and the shallot.

Cut the chicken into 1 inch pieces and pat them dry. In a bowl, toss the chicken with two thirds of the lemongrass, the garlic, the shallot, the turmeric, the salt, 1 tbsp sugar and 1 1/2 tbsp fish sauce. Leave it for 20 minutes while you do the rest.
Cut the onion into thin wedges. Seed the Fresno chilies and slice them thin. Slice the Thai chilies and put them in a small dish for the table. Chop 1/4 cup of the cilantro.

Heat the oil in a wok or large skillet over medium heat. Add the rest of the lemongrass and the Fresno chilies and stir for about 1 minute, until they smell fragrant and the lemongrass turns light golden.
Turn the heat to high and add the chicken in a single layer. Don't stir it. Let it brown underneath for 2 minutes, then stir and cook for 3 minutes, until it's browned on most sides.

Add 1/3 cup water and scrape up the browned bits. Turn the heat to medium, cover and cook for 4 minutes. You're cooking it to 175°F, so if you have a thermometer, check the biggest piece. No thermometer? Cut into it: it's done when there's no pink left.
Take off the lid and add the onion. Stir-fry for 2 minutes, until the onion is just soft and the sauce has cooked down to a sticky glaze.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the chopped cilantro. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve over the rice with the sliced Thai chilies on the side.
method_notes: The sources agree on chicken marinated in lemongrass, garlic, fish sauce and sugar, with more lemongrass and chili fried in oil first, then the chicken browned hard and finished with a short covered cook. The lead (Wok & Kin) uses wings with turmeric and bouillon powder and braises them about 30 minutes; this version uses bite-size thighs (the lead says any cut works), keeps the turmeric, drops the bouillon, and adds onion wedges as Helen Le and Luke Nguyen do. Heat is moved to the table: mild Fresno chilies go in the pan and the Thai chilies are served on the side. No source had 20 or more ratings and RecipeTin Eats has no version, so the lead is the most-rated version that could be read.
